Declare a separate output model that doesn't include the password field, and set it as the `response_model` on your path operation. FastAPI will take care of filtering out all the data that is not declared in the output model (using Pydantic).[1]

This is a common pattern for user models: the output model should not have a password[3], while the database model would probably need to have a hashed password.[3] In the docs' example, the function returns a `UserInDB` object (which has `hashed_password`), but the response uses `UserOut`:

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel, EmailStr

app = FastAPI()


class UserOut(BaseModel):
    username: str
    email: EmailStr
    full_name: str | None = None


class UserInDB(BaseModel):
    username: str
    hashed_password: str
    email: EmailStr
    full_name: str | None = None


@app.post("/user/", response_model=UserOut)
async def create_user(user_in: UserIn):
    user_saved = fake_save_user(user_in)  # returns a UserInDB
    return user_saved
```

(See the full example, including `UserIn` and `fake_save_user`, at https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/extra-models/.)

If you also annotate a return type, note that if you declare both a return type and a `response_model`, the `response_model` will take priority and be used by FastAPI.[2]

More details: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/response-model/
